units.translation: The expressions τί φημί; [what am I to say?], τί φής; [what do you say?], πῶς φής; [how do you say?], on which see Thes. vol. 8 p. 744, express astonishment.
The middle aorist form φάσθαι [to say] means to say.
But the perfect πεφασμένος [having appeared] at Pr. 842 is not to be referred to φημί [I say], as some have believed, but to φαίνομαι [I appear], as we said under φαίνω [I show].

Thus Bothius corrected for τί δ᾽ ἂν πάντες [what then would all...], and the scholiast seems to have read φάντες λεγισαι [having spoken...], who interprets: τί δεινὸν εἰπόντες κατὰ Κλυταιμνήστρας τύχοιμεν τῆς σῆς συμμαχίας [what terrible thing could we say against Clytemnestra to obtain your alliance?]
Who could say that he found silver and gold before me?
Whom shall I say I see here?
For I say that the most shameful disease is composed words.
As the prophet says.
For he says that the city will be destroyed both if the god is willing and if he is not willing.
And he says that Justice is...
What shall I say?
Ch. 778 whom you say you saw in the night.
Where do they say Athens is established on the earth?
What misfortune do you say came upon the army?
By what fate do you say these men perished?
They say that Xerxes, deserted, comes with few men.
And I say the same things, and you have me as an advocate.
For they say that the son of Alcmena was once sold and endured to obtain a slave's barley-cake.
I say that someone is planning vengeance,
I say that you will see the fate of Agamemnon.
I would say now already.
You say (thus Pauw for τόνδ᾽ ἔφης [you said this]) that he killed him willingly.
And I do not know what to say.
What shall I say?
And I say that I killed my mother not without justice.
And I say that the bold transgressor will be brought down.
What seat do you say I have?
They say that Io once became the key-holder of Hera's house.
They say that his body was fitting for a bull that feeds on oxen.
Why do you say you have come as a suppliant to these gods of the assembly?
How shall I say that I have come, and by whom was I deprived?
What would we say we have suffered, or what griefs from our parents?
Someone said that the gods do not deign to care for mortals.
I say that your head will not escape justice.
I say that you are not justly driving Orestes into exile.
And yet what am I saying?
How do you say?
What do you say?
I am eager to please, but I am also eager to speak against.
What shall I say to you or what shall I do?

The middle form φημίζομαι [I say] means I say, I speak out.
Or did Loxias say it?
You have spoken a great woe briefly.
Why have you spoken this word too piercing?
You have spoken these things following the former ones.

to anticipate, to outstrip
I anticipate with speed, I outstrip.
I fear that my great toil of wealth may become a prey to men, snatched by the one who got there first.
And having anticipated in deeds, he will leap upon him.

Destroying the wretched army of the Argives.
Destroying with their feet wealth and silver-bought robes.
